author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Barry Melrose, a former NHL player and coach who became one of ESPN’s most recognizable hockey analysts, died Wednesday at age 70, the network announced.

Melrose spent 27 years with ESPN and became known for direct commentary, deep familiarity with the sport and a distinctive on-air appearance. He left the network in 2023 after being diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.

Before broadcasting, Melrose coached the Los Angeles Kings for more than two seasons and led the Wayne Gretzky-captained team to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final. A brief later stint with the Tampa Bay Lightning brought his NHL head-coaching record to 84-108-29-4.

The Saskatchewan native also played nine professional seasons as a defenseman. He appeared in the World Hockey Association with Cincinnati and later played 300 NHL games for Winnipeg, Toronto and Detroit. ESPN described him as a foundational figure in its hockey coverage. His death is significant across the sport, including in New England, where ESPN’s Bristol studios helped make his analysis a familiar part of national NHL broadcasts.
dek: The longtime broadcaster, known for an unmistakable style and direct analysis, spent 27 years covering hockey for ESPN.
headline: Former NHL coach and ESPN analyst Barry Melrose dies at 70
